findings.question: does the report distinguish a prediction from an extrapolation?
is the interval a hypothesis was checked over recorded at all?
does an affine hypothesis die on the very next observation for non-affine data?
does the test ever falsely refute a hypothesis that is right?

findings.note: D1 predicted a rival for relu-on-{0,1,2}; there is none, because relu IS the identity there. The rival check is reported as a NEGATIVE RESULT: constrained against degeneracy it found no rival in any case, so it cannot currently distinguish a well-supported hypothesis from an unrepresentable truth.
findings.question: does the rival search do any work at all once degeneracy is excluded?
does 'no rival' get read as reassurance?
findings.wording: the rival search can only find what the ontology can represent; absence of a rival is a statement about the ontology, not about the world

findings.question: is every hypothesis under-written by a constant fitted to one point?

held_out_note: measured with a truth function in the same turn: 42/45 interpolated; the failures were a hypothesis fitted on a strictly positive range and asked about negatives, which is the domain question this module is about
